correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, the Catalan-matroid basis theorem and basis exchange reduce complete shattering to feasibility of all-on/all-off. Greedy forbidden-up-position completion proves the prefix bound, and reverse-plus-flip duality proves the suffix bound. The resulting height recursion gives a bijection to exact weighted strip walks; the tridiagonal transfer count is an integer identity, not an empirical pattern. The d=0 and d=1 specializations and the explicit n>=4 nonpure support follow algebraically. The standalone checker exhausts all supports for n<=7 and top coefficients to n=24, without claiming finite checks prove universality.

originality.rationale: The general matroid criterion, Catalan bases, and lexicographic standard complexes are existing results and are explicitly excluded from novelty. The proposed claim adds the complete Catalan ordinary-shattering coefficient census, explicit transfer/spectral formulas, exact next-to-top counts, and nonpure maximal-face witnesses. Full relevant primary material and targeted research-database and public-literature comparisons found no statement dominating these new enumerative conclusions; historical priority remains qualified by specified residual risks.
residual_risks: Priority under common-independent/coindependent-set enumerators or lattice-path-strip-walk terminology is not fully excluded; a differently named formula could subsume the stated polynomial.
The 2002 Shattering News full text was not accessible from reviewed public pages, although its abstract concerns order-shattering rather than the ordinary traces counted here.
Independent mathematical review and externally certified historical novelty are not performed.

value.rationale: An all-ranks shattering profile refines the previously known VC dimension and distinguishes ordinary shattering from order-shattering/lexicographic-standard complexes. It counts a natural learning-theoretic object exactly at every size and semilength, yields a simple computable strip transfer and spectral expression, and exposes explicitly nonpure facets of the resulting simplicial complex. The nontrivial intermediate coefficients (13,26,40,100,...) show the census is not a mere uniform-matroid binomial substitution; the full polynomial answers a motivated natural classification problem.
